name: pdk-authentik-ldap-outpost-revocation
instr:
We need LDAP outposts to reflect access changes promptly, including when a replica temporarily loses contact with authentik. In `/app`, extend the Python core and Go LDAP outpost so access changes survive a disconnected outpost and can be applied in order. PostgreSQL is available locally (`sudo service postgresql start`); the repository is at `a40205dc5525e09566b01a48c05918d762f8206c`.

An active user can bind with their LDAP DN and password. Within 10 seconds of an administrator deactivating the user through `/api/v3/core/users/`, cached binds fail on both replicas and LDAP subtree searches on both replicas stop returning the user. Within 10 seconds of a password reset through that API, the old password fails and the new password binds. Removing a user from the LDAP provider application's access group revokes existing cached binds on both replicas within 10 seconds. If a replica loses its HTTP and websocket connection to core for 20 seconds during removal, its cached bind fails within 10 seconds of reconnecting. Revocation still works within 10 seconds on both replicas while the background worker is stopped. Deactivating and reactivating a user during a disconnection leaves the recovered replica accepting the final valid credentials; a later password reset still revokes the old password within 10 seconds. An outpost built from the pinned commit still connects, receives configuration and serves an active user's bind.

Deliver source and database migration changes in the repos
